text: To see how to compose Effects properly, let us briefly return to the vile Promise. To sequence these, we define a program, mark it async, await sensor data, await biometrics, then await analyze. As we all know, calling this will execute the first promise, then the second, then the third, resolving the outer program. And now, prepare yourself. First, we'll wrap each thunk in Effect.promise. And then, I'll gesture magnificently to the right. To the left. Back to the right. Promise. Effect. Async/Await. Effect.gen. Do you see it now?
code:
const sensorData = () =>
  fetch('/api/sensors').then(r => r.json())

const biometrics = () =>
  fetch('/api/biometrics').then(r => r.json())

const analyze = (data: unknown) =>
  fetch('/api/analyze', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) })
